question.text: The rapid global growth of passive index funds is most directly justified by which implication of the Efficient Market Hypothesis?

answer.text: Indexing is superior because it always delivers higher gross returns than active management.
In an efficient market, minimising transaction costs and turnover dominates frequent trading - hence 'be with the market' via low-cost indexing improves NET returns for long-horizon investors.
EMH forbids active management under SEBI rules, so only index funds are legal.
Index funds eliminate all market, sector and macro risk for the investor.

explanation.text: The Logic: In efficient markets, minimising transaction costs is superior to frequent trading for long-horizon investors; reducing transactions lowers costs and tax implications, which is why low-cost indexing is favoured. The Trap: Option A overstates the claim to higher gross returns; Option C invents a regulatory ban on active management; Option D confuses passive management with risk elimination. Note: Source page 52 of FINAL Series XIX-C AIF Managers (Dec 2025) workbook.
